themes: Signs of resurrection in the earth
summary_for_children: Surah Al-Hajj speaks of the pilgrimage that Ibrahim proclaimed, of the House, of how rain brings dead land to life, and of worship done sincerely for Allah.
environment_concept: Roads from far mountain passes with camels (22:27), simple foundations (22:26), dry fields that turn green as rain falls (22:63) and a slope where plants stir (22:5).
architecture_and_scenery: Mountain passes feeding into a wide plain, plain stone foundations, sacrificial pastures shown only as grazing camels, and rain-fed fields.

palette.lighting: Bright sun over pale stone, rain bursts turning hills green
palette.atmosphere: Dry heat, then the scent of rain

areas.name: Roads from Every Pass
areas.description: Winding roads from far mountain passes; travellers are suggested by footprints and camel tracks only.

areas.name: Greening Fields
areas.description: Dry fields that turn green as rain falls.

areas.name: Stages of Growth
areas.description: A barren slope that stirs and swells with plants.

activities.name: Rain on the hills
activities.description: Carry rain clouds over three dry fields; they turn green.
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

activities.name: Pack for the journey
activities.description: Pack four sacks for the journey.
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

narration_plan: Narration explains Hajj simply and links rain-revived land to Allah's power to give life.
learning_objectives: Explain who first proclaimed Hajj in the surah

status.playable_environment: first version built: a composed world (foundations, herd, mountain, shoot) with 2 hands-on activities in the scene
status.testing: not tested yet: written and type-checked, not yet checked on screen

depiction_rules: No prophet, person or representation of Allah is shown. Unseen realities are never pictured. Interactive activities are labelled as adaptations.

unique_world.visual_theme: A wide desert valley ringed by hills with passes, and a map model on a stone plinth in the middle

primary_mechanic.text: Four carved stones each tell one step that 22:26-29 gives (the House made ready, the call and travellers from every distant pass, remembering Allah and feeding the poor, vows kept and the ancient House). Carry them to the map model and set them in the order of the verses; a stone set too early is handed back. Each stone changes the model.

unique_world.narrative_structure: Find and set the four stones in order, then the lantern by the path
world_assets: map model with hills, passes and paths
a plain round marker for the site of the House (no Kaaba replica)
environment_behaviour: the House marker turns clean and pale
small lights travel along the passes (no people)
a soft ring of light around the marker
unique_world.learning_objective: Learn the order the pilgrimage verses give and that what reaches Allah is the mindfulness of the heart (22:37)

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Journey of Pilgrimage
story_library.children_narration: The Quran reminds us of the Sacred House and the pilgrimage. People come from distant places to worship Allah, remember Him, and carry out acts of devotion. The surah teaches that what matters is not simply an outward action but sincere faith and mindfulness of Allah.

world_idea.title: The Pilgrimage Journey
world_idea.description: Explore a carefully researched sacred-landscape learning environment, practice recognizing locations and the order of pilgrimage activities, and learn why each matters. Avoid turning worship into a competitive challenge.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: No replica of the Kaaba or the Sacred Mosque; the stations are a simple map model. Reviewers should decide what may be shown.
